newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, December expires smoothly.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, December expires smoothly.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mixed after a thinly traded session, and the nearby December contract expired smoothly, traders said.
Nearbys gained in part, on firmness in Argentine cash values, while new crop contracts lost ground as concerns faded about cold weather damage to the U.S. HRW crop.

"We had an uneventful, ordinary expiration of the December contract amid local selling that drove down the July," a KCBT trader said. "The overall strength in grains has come off the fact that problematic situations in Argentina are prompting higher prices there."
KCBT wheat closed 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 3-1/2 cents higher, with Dec up 3-1/2 cents at $4.67. March gained 1/4 cent to close at $4.15-1/2.
Traders said early gains were limited by hedge selling tied to an increase in farmer selling of wheat.
Traders said LFG had bought at least 1.2 million March bushels, probably on the spread with CBOT wheat. CIS sold 1.6 million March.
